t: Under Section 3 of the Employees' Compensation Act, the employer is NOT liable for an injury (not resulting in death or permanent total disablement) caused by:
o: Lack of skill of the worker
The worker being under the influence of drink or drugs, or wilful disobedience of safety rules, or wilful removal of safety guards
e: The defences in the proviso to Section 3(1) are drink/drugs, wilful disobedience of express safety orders and wilful removal of safety guards; they do not apply where the injury results in death or permanent total disablement.

t: A claim for relief under the Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991 is made to the:
e: Applications for relief are made to the Collector of the district, who holds an inquiry and makes an award; the application must be filed within five years of the accident.

t: The period of limitation under the Limitation Act, 1963 for a civil suit against an insurer on a policy of insurance is:
e: Article 44 of the Schedule to the Limitation Act provides three years for suits against an insurer on a policy, running from the occurrence of the loss or the date the claim is denied.

t: When a cover note is not followed by a policy within the specified time, the insurer's notification under Section 147 goes to:
o: The registering authority or such other authority as the State Government may prescribe
The Regional Transport Officer of the insurer's head office
e: The notification must be made to the registering authority in whose records the vehicle is registered, or to any other authority prescribed by the State Government.

topic: MV Act s.147 – Limits of liability
t: Under the un-amended Section 147(2)(a), the policy must cover liability for death or bodily injury of a third party up to:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Section 147(2)(a) required cover for 'the amount of liability incurred', i.e. unlimited, whereas clause (b) fixed ₹6,000 for third-party property damage.

t: The pecuniary jurisdiction of Consumer Commissions under the 2019 Act is determined by:
o: The value of goods or services paid as consideration
The sum insured under the policy
The net worth of the opposite party
The compensation claimed in the complaint
e: Unlike the 1986 Act (value of goods plus compensation claimed), the 2019 Act uses the value of goods or services paid as consideration, which for insurance means the premium.

t: Under IRDAI's 2024 norms, a surveyor must be appointed within what time of a claim intimation?
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Appointment within 24 hours; survey report within 15 days; insurer's decision within 7 days of the report.

t: An arbitral award on quantum under a fire policy is received by the insurer on 1 April. An application to set it aside under Section 34 must ordinarily be filed within:
o: 3 months, extendable by a further 30 days
e: Section 34(3) requires the application within three months of receipt of the award; the court may condone a further 30 days but not thereafter.

t: A general insurer settles a claim 60 days after the date it should have been paid under the regulations. Under the PPHI framework the insurer must pay interest on the delayed amount at:
o: 2% above the bank rate prevailing at the beginning of the financial year
e: The policyholder-protection regulations require insurers to pay interest at 2% above the bank rate for delays beyond the prescribed timelines, over and above the claim amount.

t: Under Section 12 of the PMLA read with the Rules, records of transactions and identity of clients must be maintained by an insurer for:
o: 5 years from the transaction / end of business relationship
e: Reporting entities must maintain transaction records for five years from the date of transaction and identity records for five years after the business relationship ends.

t: Which of the following was newly brought within 'unfair trade practice' by the 2019 Act?
o: Disclosure of a consumer's personal information given in confidence, unless permitted by law
e: The 2019 Act's broad definition of unfair trade practice specifically includes sharing personal information given by the consumer in confidence, unless such disclosure is made under any other law.

t: A fleet owner's contract with a logistics company makes him liable to pay ₹5 lakh for every late delivery caused by an accident. Under Section 147(1), the motor policy:
o: Must cover this liability as it arises from use of the vehicle
Must cover it if the vehicle is a goods carriage
Is not required to cover any contractual liability
Must cover it up to ₹6,000 only
e: Proviso (ii) to Section 147(1) states that a policy is not required to cover any contractual liability.

t: The amended Section 147(2) refers to prescribing a base premium for third-party insurance in respect of:
o: Death or grievous hurt to a person
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). The amended sub-section covers third-party insurance related to either death of a person or grievous hurt, for which the Central Government prescribes a base premium and insurer's liability.

t: A Public Information Officer of a PSU insurer replies to an RTI application 50 days after receipt without reasonable cause. The penalty the Information Commission may impose is:
o: ₹250 per day for the 20 days' delay, i.e. ₹5,000
₹250 per day for all 50 days, i.e. ₹12,500
e: Section 7 requires a reply within 30 days; Section 20 imposes ₹250 per day of delay, subject to a maximum of ₹25,000. The delay is 20 days, so ₹5,000.

t: Section 147(5)/(6) provides that, notwithstanding any other law, an insurer issuing a policy under the section shall:
o: Be liable to indemnify the persons specified in the policy for the liability it purports to cover
Be liable only after the insured pays the award
Be liable only up to the premium collected
Have no liability if the insured breaches policy conditions
e: The sub-section makes the insurer liable to indemnify the person or classes of persons specified in the policy in respect of any liability the policy purports to cover, overriding any other law.

topic: MV Act s.147 – Certificate of insurance
t: Under Section 147(3), the certificate of insurance must contain:
o: The prescribed particulars of any condition subject to which the policy is issued and other prescribed matters
The claim history of the insured
e: The certificate must be in the prescribed form, containing particulars of any condition subject to which the policy is issued and any other prescribed matters; different forms may be prescribed for different cases.

t: The Explanation to Section 2(7) relating to 'commercial purpose' applies to:
o: Goods bought and used exclusively for earning a livelihood by self-employment
e: The Explanation clarifies that for sub-clause (i) (goods), 'commercial purpose' does not include use by a consumer of goods bought and used exclusively for earning his livelihood by means of self-employment.

t: The 'golden hour' under Section 2(12A) of the amended MV Act means:
o: The hour within which the police must reach the spot
The hour within which the insurer must appoint a surveyor
The one-hour period following a traumatic injury during which prompt medical care is most likely to prevent death
e: Section 2(12A) defines golden hour as the one-hour period following a traumatic injury; Section 162 requires schemes for cashless treatment of victims during this period.

t: Section 14 of the IRDA Act, 1999 confers on the Authority the duty to:
o: Underwrite risks of the PSU insurers
Fix tariffs for all classes of insurance
Regulate, promote and ensure orderly growth of the insurance business and reinsurance business
e: Section 14 lists IRDAI's duties, powers and functions, including issuing registration, protecting policyholders, regulating intermediaries and ensuring orderly growth.

t: Under the proviso to the old Section 147(2), a limited-liability policy in force immediately before commencement of the 1988 Act continued to be effective for:
o: Till expiry of the policy in all cases
Four months after commencement or till expiry, whichever earlier
e: The transitional proviso allowed such policies to continue for four months after commencement of the Act or till the date of expiry of the policy, whichever was earlier.

t: Under the IRDAI (Protection of Policyholders' Interests) Regulations 2024, the free-look period for a policy with a term of one year or more is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). 30 days from receipt of the policy document, irrespective of the sales channel.

t: The Explanation to Section 147(1) was inserted 'for the removal of doubts' to clarify that:
o: Only accidents on highways are covered
The victim need not be in a public place if the act or omission leading to the accident occurred in a public place
Passengers of goods vehicles are excluded
e: The Explanation deems death, injury or property damage to arise out of use in a public place even if the victim or property was not in a public place, provided the causative act occurred in a public place.

t: The minimum paid-up equity capital required to start a life or general insurance company in India is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). ₹100 crore for a direct insurer; ₹200 crore for a reinsurer (Section 6 of the Insurance Act).

topic: MV Act s.147 – Requirements of policy
t: Section 147(1)(a) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 requires that a policy complying with Chapter XI must be issued by:
o: An insurer approved by the State Transport Authority
Any insurer registered with the Registrar of Companies
e: Section 147(1)(a) mandates that the policy be issued by a person who is an 'authorised insurer', a term defined in Section 145.

t: Under the 1986 Act a complaint was ordinarily filed at the place of purchase or the seller's registered office. The 2019 Act changed this by permitting filing:
o: Only at the place of the opposite party's branch
At the place where the consumer resides or works
e: The 2019 Act gives the consumer the flexibility to file at the jurisdictional Commission of his place of residence or work.

t: The maximum waiting period for pre-existing diseases in health insurance, after the 2024 IRDAI changes, is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Reduced from 48 to 36 months; the moratorium period after which claims cannot be contested (except fraud) is 60 months.

t: Section 124 of the Indian Contract Act defines a contract of indemnity as one by which one party promises to:
o: Pay a fixed sum on an event
Save the other from loss caused by the conduct of the promisor himself or any other person
e: Section 124 defines indemnity as a promise to save the other party from loss caused by the promisor or any other person; non-life insurance follows the indemnity principle.

t: The 2019 Act fixes liability on endorsers of advertisements primarily because:
o: Endorsers are treated as product manufacturers
Advertising agencies are not legal persons
Endorsers receive a share of sales revenue
Consumers have fallen prey to unfair trade practices under the influence of celebrities, so endorsers must exercise due diligence
e: The Act expects endorsers to verify the veracity of claims they endorse; absent due diligence they share liability for misleading advertisements.

t: An insurer's solvency ratio falls to 130%. Under Section 64VA and IRDAI norms the insurer:
o: Has breached the 150% control level and must submit a financial plan to IRDAI
e: The control level of solvency is 150%; an insurer below it must submit a financial plan to IRDAI, which may restrict its business.

t: Compared with a product seller or service provider, the liability of a product manufacturer under the 2019 Act is:
o: Lower, since manufacturers are regulated by BIS
Higher, as the manufacturer is liable even without negligence or fraud in an express warranty
Nil if the product carries an ISI mark
e: The Act imposes stricter liability on manufacturers, who cannot escape by proving absence of negligence or fraud in making an express warranty, while sellers have defences such as misuse or alteration.
